overview: Goodman Group is an ASX-listed stapled entity (Goodman Limited, Goodman Industrial Trust, and Goodman Logistics (HK) Limited, quoted as a single security) that owns, develops and manages industrial/logistics real estate and, increasingly, data centres across Asia Pacific, Continental Europe, the UK and the Americas. It operates an integrated 'own-develop-manage' model, investing alongside large institutional capital Partners (sovereign wealth, pension and multi-manager funds) rather than holding all assets on its own balance sheet. With a $89.0 billion total portfolio and $75.4 billion of assets under management as at 30 June 2026, it is the largest property group listed on the ASX and one of the world's largest specialist industrial/digital infrastructure investment managers.

business_model.summary: Goodman earns three distinct but complementary streams from a single integrated platform: (1) property investment income from directly held assets and its equity share of Partnership portfolios (rental income net of costs); (2) management earnings — base management fees on assets under management plus property services fees and transaction/performance fees from managing capital on behalf of institutional Partners; and (3) development earnings — profits from developing land into logistics facilities and (increasingly) data centres, either sold/transferred into Partnerships or retained. Development has become the dominant and fastest-growing earnings stream, reflecting the data centre build-out, while management earnings (historically the most fee-like/recurring stream) fell in FY26 due to lower performance fees.

revenue_streams.name: Management earnings (base fees, property services, performance/transaction fees)
Property investment earnings (direct + Partnership rental income)

business_model.customer_type: B2B — e-commerce, logistics, retail, manufacturing, pharmaceutical/life sciences customers for warehouses; hyperscale cloud/AI providers for data centres; institutional investors (sovereign wealth, pension, multi-manager funds) as capital Partners
business_model.geographic_mix: Portfolio value: Australia/NZ $39.3bn (44%), Asia $24.1bn (27%, incl. Greater China, Hong Kong, Japan), Europe/UK $13.9bn (16%), Americas $11.7bn (13%). Partnership AUM roughly: ANZ 43%, Asia 31%, UK/Continental Europe 16%, Americas 10%.

main_competitors: Digital Realty and Equinix (data centre/digital infrastructure segment)
competitive_position.market_position: Largest property group listed on the ASX (top-20 by market cap) and one of the world's largest listed specialist managers of industrial property and digital infrastructure. Global leader among ASX-listed peers in scale of logistics land bank and cross-border development capability; among the ASX REITs, Charter Hall is the closest structural analogue (stapled, funds-management-led model), while Digital Realty/Equinix are the more relevant global competitors in the emerging data centre business.

moat_factors.description: Decades of accumulated metro-adjacent industrial land positions Goodman uniquely to convert sites to logistics or low-latency data centres where new land is scarce and planning approvals are slow

6.4 GW global power bank (3.6 GW secured, 2.8 GW in advanced procurement) across 16 major cities — energy access, not capital, is the binding constraint on data centre supply, and Goodman controls a scarce pipeline of it

In-house land acquisition, power procurement, planning, construction and leasing capability, plus ~300 staff dedicated to data centre delivery, differentiates Goodman from pure-play REITs or pure developers

Long-standing relationships with sovereign wealth, pension and multi-manager Partners provide access to $75B+ of AUM and third-party capital that reduces balance-sheet risk, though it is not unique to Goodman among stapled peers
Multi-decade record of logistics development and 25%+ ROE culture supports customer and capital-partner trust, but does not by itself prevent competitors replicating strategy given enough capital

weaknesses: Data centre business is unproven at scale — no meaningful stabilised data centre income yet; earnings depend on future leasing outcomes 2-3 years out
Falling pre-commitment rates on WIP (25% pre-committed at 30 June 2026 vs 49% a year earlier) increase speculative development and leasing risk
Management (fee) earnings — the most recurring, capital-light stream — actually declined 17.6% in FY26 on lower performance fees, showing volatility even in the 'annuity' segment

Heavy reliance on continued third-party capital availability to fund an expanding $19.7bn WIP book; global data centre capex demand may outstrip available capital markets funding, per management's own commentary
China portfolio weak — valuation losses and subdued leasing conditions persisting across FY25-FY26

growth_drivers: Data centre pivot: 78% of $19.7bn development WIP is now data centres (up from 57% in FY25), driven by AI/cloud compute demand, with 0.5 GW of powered shell/fully fitted capacity in WIP and $15.4bn of total data centre WIP
Global power bank expansion to 6.4 GW (from 5.0 GW in FY25), providing a scarce, hard-to-replicate resource base for future data centre conversions
Shift of AI workloads from training to inference concentrating demand in supply-constrained metro markets — precisely where Goodman's urban-infill land bank sits
New capital Partnerships (four added in FY26, ~$3.2bn of third-party equity raised) including a 50:50 North American JV with DataBank giving access to 2,000+ hyperscale/enterprise customers
Continued conversion of existing industrial sites to data centre use, expanding long-term development capacity without new land acquisition
Ongoing logistics demand from automation/robotics adoption requiring large-scale, power-enabled modern warehouse facilities
Low gearing (6.5%, within 0-25% target range) and $6.4bn liquidity (plus $6.7bn at Partnership level) provide capacity to fund the growth pipeline without near-term equity dilution risk

business.description: Only 25% of WIP was pre-committed at FY26 year-end (vs 49% prior year); most projects reach 'ready for service' in CY2028, exposing Goodman to a multi-year lag between committing capital and securing tenants in a market that could soften

business.risk: Concentration in a single structural theme
business.description: Group earnings are increasingly levered to one thesis (AI/cloud compute demand for data centres); a slowdown in hyperscaler capex or AI infrastructure spend would disproportionately affect Goodman versus diversified REIT peers
Mainland China logistics portfolio recorded valuation losses and subdued leasing in both FY25 and FY26, a drag on an otherwise strong global book

Rival REITs and global data centre operators (Digital Realty, Equinix, ESR) are actively competing for the same industrial and data centre land and power capacity, potentially compressing future returns on invested capital

financial.description: Gearing increased from 4.3% to 6.5% in FY26 as development activity intensified; still low versus the 0-25% target range but the trajectory is upward alongside a rapidly growing WIP book

Significant offshore earnings (Asia, Europe, Americas ~56% of portfolio) create translation risk; a stronger AUD reduced FY26 management and property investment earnings from overseas operations, partially offset by hedging (65-90% of net investment in major overseas operations is hedged)

Share-based payment expense (LTIP) was $465.8m in FY26, a large and growing non-cash item that creates a wide gap between operating and statutory profit and is sensitive to security price and performance hurdle achievement

regulatory.risk: Data centre planning and community backlash
regulatory.description: Management itself has acknowledged that some data centre proposals may never proceed due to community opposition, environmental policy and planning hurdles; regulatory approval timelines for power and construction are a genuine constraint, not just a formality

Energy availability is explicitly cited by management as 'the most significant constraint' on delivering digital infrastructure — grid connection queues, transformer lead times (industry-wide ~128 weeks) and power allocation policy can delay or derail projects
GIT's flow-through trust taxation and the stapled structure are subject to ongoing Australian tax policy risk common to all ASX stapled REITs

macro.risk: Interest rate sensitivity via cap rates
macro.description: Portfolio valuations are highly sensitive to capitalisation rates; FY26 valuation gains were driven substantially by cap rate compression (5.08% to 4.96%), which would reverse if rates rise or risk premia widen

macro.risk: Global data centre capex funding gap
macro.description: Management notes capital required to meet forecast global data centre demand is expected to exceed the funding capacity of global capital markets — a macro constraint that could slow the pace of Partnership capital raising industry-wide
Global trade conditions moderated customer decision-making in logistics leasing in H2 FY26; geopolitical tension also affects construction costs and supply chains for development projects

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Structural, multi-decade demand tailwind from e-commerce, automation/robotics in logistics, and explosive AI/cloud-driven demand for data centre capacity, concentrated in supply-constrained metro markets; industry-wide, power/grid delays are causing roughly $150-200bn of global data centre capex to slip from 2026 into 2027-2028, which could either validate Goodman's power-bank moat or signal broader execution risk across the sector
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high — industrial/logistics rents are relatively resilient, but development earnings (now >55% of Group earnings) are inherently cyclical and transaction-timing dependent; property valuations are directly exposed to interest rate/cap rate cycles
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High — as a capital-intensive global property developer/owner-manager, both portfolio valuations (via cap rates) and cost of capital for its own and Partnership development funding are directly affected by rate movements

recent_developments.event: FY26 results: operating profit up 15.7% to $2,674.5m, operating EPS up 10.1% to 129.9c; data centres now 78% of $19.7bn development WIP (up from 57% in FY25); gearing rose from 4.3% to 6.5%; shares traded down ~1.2% on results day amid investor caution over revenue-recognition timing of the data centre pipeline
Issued US$1.2bn and €600.0m of new notes via 144A/Reg S bond market, extending weighted average debt maturity to 7.5 years and boosting liquidity to $6.4bn

Established new data centre development Partnerships in Continental Europe and North America, including a 50:50 operational/development JV with DataBank giving access to 2,000+ existing customers; four new capital Partnerships added overall, ~$3.2bn third-party equity raised

Signed a 20-year, 50MW lease with a major hyperscale customer at the TYO05 (Tokyo) data centre project; advanced negotiations for additional capacity and several other major long-term leases expected to be announced 'in coming months'
Established Goodman U.S. Value Partnership (GUSV), transferring $1.4bn of North American properties out of the directly held stabilised portfolio, reported as a disposal
Disposed of Moorabbin Airport properties from the AUM base

Growing public and community backlash against data centre developments in several markets; CEO Greg Goodman publicly acknowledged some proposed projects may never proceed due to planning/community opposition

Analyst commentary split: consensus remains Buy (9 buy, 5 strong buy, 3 hold among ~17 analysts) with average price targets around A$34-36, while at least one major research house (Morningstar) maintains a more cautious fair value near A$29, flagging returns-on-invested-capital risk as competition in data centres intensifies

guidance.as_of: FY26 Annual Results / Chairman and CEO letter, 19 August 2026

items.notes: Management expects earnings to be weighted toward the second half of FY27, reflecting timing of project completions, leasing and asset transfers
Distribution held flat for a second consecutive year to retain capital for the expanding development program while keeping gearing within the 0-25% target range
WIP grew 53% in FY26 to $19.7bn; management expects further growth in FY27 given projects anticipated to commence over the coming year

items.target: Majority of current WIP data centre projects reach first RFS in calendar 2028
items.notes: Leasing/commercial negotiations continuing in parallel with construction; management expects to announce several leasing transactions 'in the coming months'

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Greg Goodman and Chairman Stephen Johns characterised FY26 as reflecting five years of deliberate repositioning toward 'essential infrastructure for the digital economy,' citing AI adoption accelerating against constrained global compute capacity, with energy availability described as 'the most significant constraint' on delivery. Management explicitly flagged that capital required to meet global data centre demand is expected to exceed the funding capacity of global capital markets — framed as an opportunity for a well-capitalised, low-geared incumbent like Goodman, but also a signal of stretched sector-wide funding needs. The FY27 outlook is described as entering the year 'with an attractive and substantial development workbook' and 'a strong capital position to support future growth.'

bull_case: Uniquely positioned land bank and 6.4 GW power bank in supply-constrained metro markets give Goodman a structural head start in monetising the AI/cloud data centre boom that is difficult for competitors to replicate quickly

Conservative balance sheet (6.5% gearing, $6.4bn liquidity, 7.5-year average debt maturity, no maturities in the next 12 months) provides ample capacity to fund the pipeline without near-term dilutive equity raising

Diversified three-pillar earnings model (property investment, management, development) across four global regions reduces reliance on any single market or income stream, with development earnings already validating the data centre strategy (up 33.9% in FY26)

Strong institutional capital partner network ($75.4bn AUM, four new Partnerships added in FY26) de-risks funding by sharing capital intensity of data centre builds with sovereign wealth, pension and multi-manager investors
Logistics fundamentals remain resilient globally (95.6% occupancy, 4.0% like-for-like rental growth) even as the data centre growth option compounds on top of a proven core business
bear_case: Data centre earnings are largely unproven and forward-looking: only 25% of $19.7bn WIP was pre-committed at FY26 year-end, and most projects don't reach ready-for-service until CY2028 — a multi-year window in which AI infrastructure demand could soften before completion

Rising gearing (4.3% to 6.5% in one year) alongside a rapidly expanding, increasingly speculative development book raises execution and funding risk if capital markets tighten or leasing assumptions don't materialise

Intensifying competition from both ASX REIT peers (Charter Hall, Dexus, GPT, Mirvac) replicating the stapled funds-management model and specialist global data centre operators (Digital Realty, Equinix, ESR) could compress future returns on invested capital, as flagged by at least one major analyst house maintaining a materially lower fair value (~A$29) than consensus targets (~A$34-36)

Regulatory and community backlash against data centre developments is a real and growing constraint — management has itself acknowledged some proposed projects may never be built — while energy/grid delays are an industry-wide bottleneck (roughly $150-200bn of global data centre capex reportedly slipping into 2027-2028)

Management (fee) earnings, the most annuity-like and capital-light income stream, actually fell 17.6% in FY26 on lower performance fees — a reminder that even the 'recurring' part of Goodman's business is more volatile than a typical REIT rent roll, and property valuations remain sensitive to interest rate/cap rate reversals after several years of compression-driven gains
